issues.legal_issue: An exemption relating to land may remove the specified land-reform restrictions even when granted after the land has been acquired.
material_facts: The land was purchased before the State Government granted an exemption relating to that land from specified restrictions on landholding and transfers.
The proposed use was a clay-processing industrial unit, a type of use for which the Government could grant an exemption.
The High Court treated the exemption as ineffective because it was granted after the purchase and found the acquisition contrary to the restrictions.
The Supreme Court held that the exemption concerned the land, could be granted before or after acquisition, and made examination of compliance with those restrictions unnecessary.
issues.conclusion: The post-purchase exemption was effective in relation to the land, so the High Court's finding that the acquisition contravened the specified land-reform restrictions was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 109 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, the State Government may exempt land from Sections 63, 79A, 79B and 80 for specified uses, including industrial purposes, or in the public interest. Because the exemption is with reference to the land rather than a particular person or transaction, it may be granted before acquisition or when the land is later put to an eligible use. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.appeal_from_writ_ruling: A party appeals a writ-court ruling that the acquisition or holding of land contravenes land-reform restrictions.
predicates.land_specific_exemption_granted: The government grants an exemption that relates to the land rather than to a particular person or transaction.
predicates.proposed_use_is_eligible_for_exemption: The land is intended for a use for which an exemption may be granted.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a writ ruling and the government has exempted the land for an eligible use, the specified land restrictions do not apply to that land.

issues.legal_issue: A transaction alleged to contravene land-reform restrictions does not itself cause the land to vest in the State without the prescribed enforcement process.
material_facts: The High Court considered whether the purchase contravened restrictions on who could acquire or hold agricultural land and transfer restrictions.
The relevant provisions contemplated declarations, enquiries and subsequent orders or notifications before land could vest in the State.
No enforcement proceedings under those provisions had been initiated in this case.
issues.conclusion: Land does not vest in the State merely because a transaction is entered into in contravention of the restrictions; the prescribed enquiry and an appropriate order are required.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 79(4), 79B and 80 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, provide for the prescribed enforcement steps where their restrictions are contravened. Depending on the provision, those steps include obtaining particulars or a declaration, holding an enquiry, and making an order or notification before vesting and taking possession. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.land_restriction_breach_alleged: A party alleges that a land transaction or holding contravenes a restriction on acquiring, holding or transferring agricultural land.
predicates.land_reform_enforcement_proceeding: The case concerns enforcement of statutory restrictions on acquiring, holding or transferring agricultural land.
predicates.prescribed_inquiry_or_order_required: The applicable enforcement process requires an inquiry, declaration, order or notification before the land can vest in the State.

issues.definition: In an enforcement proceeding, an alleged breach does not itself cause State vesting when the applicable process requires an inquiry or order first.

issues.legal_issue: Environmental and other clearances for a proposed industrial unit that has not commenced operation must be freshly assessed when new clearances are sought.
material_facts: The proposed clay-processing unit had not been commissioned and was not carrying out any activity.
The State stated that earlier pollution-control and factory clearances were being withdrawn and that steps to withdraw them were being initiated.
The Union alleged that the land included an area covered by a forest-department plantation and was surrounded by reserve-forest areas.
The Court did not decide whether the unit could be established and left the parties free to pursue or oppose it.
The Court directed the authorities to make a fresh assessment, taking account of environmental and ecological protections, if new clearances were sought.
issues.conclusion: The Court left the merits of the proposed unit open and directed the authorities to undertake a fresh assessment under the applicable environmental and ecological enactments before granting any clearances sought by the appellants.
issues.legal_principle: Clearances must be given only after appropriate enquiry or assessment that takes account of enactments protecting the environment and ecology. Where a unit is not operating and fresh clearances are required, earlier clearances may not be of use; the authorities must assess the matter afresh. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.appeal_concerning_proposed_industrial_un: The proceeding concerns an appeal relating to a proposed industrial unit and its clearances.
predicates.unit_not_commissioned: The proposed unit has not begun operating.
predicates.earlier_clearances_not_reliable_for_curr: Earlier clearances have been withdrawn, are being withdrawn, or may no longer support the proposed operation.
predicates.new_clearance_sought: The party proposing the unit asks the authorities for a new clearance.
predicates.authorities_must_freshly_assess_environm: The authorities must assess the applicable environmental and ecological requirements afresh before granting a clearance.

issues.definition: When an uncommissioned industrial unit seeks new clearances and its earlier clearances cannot support current operation, the authorities must assess environmental and ecological requirements afresh.
